subject: general
question: What happens when you delete a file or folder using the Delete key?

options.text: The file is copied to another folder.
The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.
The file is permanently deleted without warning.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you delete a file or folder using the **Delete key** on a Windows computer, the file is not permanently deleted. Instead, it is sent to the **Recycle Bin.**
 
• The **Recycle Bin** serves as a temporary storage location for deleted files, allowing users to restore files that may have been deleted accidentally.
 
• Files remain in the **Recycle Bin** until the user manually empties it or it reaches its storage limit, after which the oldest files are removed automatically.
 
• This feature acts as a safeguard against accidental deletion and ensures that users have the ability to recover important files if needed.
 
• To permanently delete a file without moving it to the Recycle Bin, users can use the **Shift + Delete** keyboard shortcut.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is typically accessible from the desktop, and users can review and restore files by right-clicking on them and selecting the **Restore** option.
 
• The functionality of the **Recycle Bin** is a built-in feature of Windows operating systems and is widely used to manage deleted files efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The file is copied to another folder.**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because deleting a file does not copy it to another folder.
 
• Copying a file requires a separate action, such as using the **Ctrl + C** and **Ctrl + V** keyboard shortcuts or the context menu options.
 
 
 
• **The file is renamed automatically.**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because deleting a file does not rename it automatically.
 
• Renaming a file requires the user to manually select the file, right-click on it, and choose the **Rename** option or use the **F2 key**.
 
 
 
• **The file is permanently deleted without warning.**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because files deleted using the **Delete key** are not permanently removed.
 
• Permanently deleting files typically involves using the **Shift + Delete** keyboard combination, bypassing the **Recycle Bin**.
